deviations: Gate 27.1 design clarification discovered during implementation: an onlyPdfs (per-PDF worker) run executes ONLY its selected PDFs' loop — the deferred tail (validation, DOX, workspace, cross-wiki, updater, end-of-run state/metrics) is the finalize worker's alone (vision-consistent: 'the deferred tail runs in its own worker exactly once after the loop'). Without this cut, every per-PDF worker would re-run the whole DOX pass (divergent AND expensive). Gate 27.1 proves the true conductor shape (PDF worker, PDF worker, finalize run) converges byte-for-byte to the single full run's durable tree (run-window artifacts excluded: metrics, llm-calls, transport-stalls, validation-report, conflicts).

Gate 27.1's crash gates exercise the conductor via a scripted SpawnWorkerFn (deterministic spawn outcomes) rather than the PAPER_CHASE_WORKER_FAULT env var — the env-var path is wired in the worker subcommand (workerFaultAfterProgress/workerFaultBeforeResult) and is what the LIVE human UAT 27.1 uses; the scripted gates assert the same outcome shapes (no result event + non-zero close) that the env var produces.

watchItems: The finalize worker is still one long-lived process (hours on a 37-PDF wiki) — acceptable per the ratified design, but if it ever becomes the crash exposure, it can be split later (per-level DOX workers) under a new amendment.

A single giant PDF still runs ~a day in one worker; memory is bounded per PDF but the within-PDF growth curve was never measured (the rkkp post-mortem measured cross-PDF growth). If a single-PDF OOM ever fires, the crash panel + retry absorbs it; a within-PDF memory fix would be Solution 3 territory.
The crash panel's Skip is intentionally absent for finalize crashes (deferral applies to PDFs only); finalize crash = Retry or Abort, per the never-auto-defer law.
